patients.summary: Retired construction foreman and former 40 pack-year smoker who joins in 2019 with hypertension, stage 2 CKD, BPH, lumbar spondylosis and a urethral stricture. Over seven years he collects chronic bronchitis, Paget disease of the left tibia, JAK2-positive primary myelofibrosis on ruxolitinib, age-related cognitive decline, a resolved L4 radiculopathy, stricture-related hematuria, carotid sinus hypersensitivity, and an ICU stay for hypertensive emergency complicated by nitroprusside cyanide toxicity.

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
64M new to the practice, transferring from a retiring PCP. Records reviewed (see outside records 9/10).

HTN: on HCTZ 25 and lisinopril 10 for about ten years. Doesn't check at home. No headaches, chest pain, SOB.
CKD 2: told of protein in the urine a few years back, creatinine has been ~1.1. No NSAIDs other than an occasional ibuprofen years ago; uses Tylenol now.
BPH: tamsulosin at night, gets up once. Stream weak through the spring, which turned out to be the stricture; urology dilated it 8/12 and he says the stream is the best it's been in years.
Back: lumbar arthritis, decades of hauling and framing. Had pain down a leg years ago that settled. Now just stiffness in the mornings, Tylenol a few times a week.

PSH: appendectomy at 34. Cysto with urethral dilation 8/2019.
FH: father MI at 68. Mother had dementia, difficult behaviors toward the end. Older brother has Paget disease of bone.
SH: married. Retired foreman. Smokes about a pack a day since his early twenties, 40 pack-years. Has quit twice for a few weeks. Beer a couple of times a month.
Allergies: NKDA.

Exam: BP 134/84. Well-appearing, heavyset. HEENT ok. Neck supple, no bruits. Heart RRR, no murmur. Lungs clear, no wheeze. Abd soft, nontender, no masses or organomegaly. Ext no edema. Back: mild paraspinal tenderness low lumbar, SLR negative both sides, strength and reflexes symmetric.

A/P
1. HTN, at goal on current regimen. Continue. CMP today.
2. CKD stage 2 with albuminuria. Already on ACE inhibitor. UACR, CMP.
3. BPH / urethral stricture, voiding well post dilation. PSA today with his agreement after talking through pros and cons.
4. Lumbar spondylosis, stable. Acetaminophen PRN, avoid NSAIDs given kidneys.
5. Tobacco: long talk. Not ready to set a date but will think about it over the holidays. Eligible for yearly low-dose CT screening, ordered.
6. HM: Tdap today. HCV and HIV once. Colonoscopy 2014 normal, due 2024. Flu shot when the high-dose arrives.

RTC 6 months.

documents.title: Pulmonology Consultation
documents.author: pulmonology
documents.body:
Outside pulmonary clinic
Date of service: 04/18/2022
Re: Bernard Bennett, DOB 07/03/1955
Referring: primary care

Thank you for asking us to see Mr. Bennett for cough.

He has brought up phlegm most days for about two years, always worse through the cold months. The sputum is white; for roughly the last four months it has been streaked with blood on and off. He has had no fevers, no weight loss and no night sweats.

History: hypertension, chronic kidney disease, BPH, urethral stricture (dilated 2019), lumbar spondylosis. Appendectomy. Meds: hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg, lisinopril 10 mg, tamsulosin 0.4 mg, acetaminophen as needed. NKDA.
Family: father MI at 68; mother dementia; brother with Paget disease of bone.
Social: retired construction foreman. Former smoker, 40 pack-years, quit in 2020. Rare alcohol.

Exam: BP 135/85, HR 78, SpO2 96% on room air. Overweight gentleman, comfortable. Scattered wheezes throughout with a prolonged expiratory phase. No crackles. Heart regular. No clubbing or edema.

Chest radiograph today, PA/lateral: increased bronchovascular markings; no mass, no focal consolidation.
Screening low-dose CTs 2019-2021 were all negative.

Impression: Chronic bronchitis in a former heavy smoker. The blood streaking fits airway inflammation, and there is no radiographic or recent CT sign of a mass.

Recommendations:
- Remain tobacco free.
- Continue annual low-dose CT screening; next due November.
- Call if he coughs up more than streaks, or with fever or weight loss.
- Follow up with us as needed.

Allergies reviewed: NKDA.
Pulmonary consultant

documents.title: Orthopedic Consultation
documents.author: orthopedics
documents.body:
Outside orthopedic practice
Visit 10/24/2022
Patient: Bernard Bennett, 67 y/o M

Reason for referral: left leg pain.

Mr. Bennett describes six months of left leg pain that keeps getting worse. He points from the hip down along the front of the shin. More recently he has had headaches and finds he hears less on the right.

PMH: HTN, CKD, BPH, urethral stricture, lumbar arthritis, chronic bronchitis (pulmonary, spring 2022). Former smoker, 40 pack-years, quit 2020. Retired construction foreman; occasional alcohol.
Meds: HCTZ 25 mg, lisinopril 10 mg, tamsulosin 0.4 mg, acetaminophen PRN. NKDA.
FH: notable for an older brother with Paget disease of bone.

Exam: Left hip moves fully without pain. The left tibia is enlarged and warm to touch with mild erythema; the skin over it is otherwise unchanged. Neurologic exam is unremarkable apart from reduced hearing on the right.

Labs today: calcium 9.8 mg/dL, phosphorus 3.5 mg/dL, alkaline phosphatase 220 U/L (H), intact PTH 55 pg/mL, 25-OH vitamin D 32 ng/mL.
Radiographs left tibia/fibula: cortical thickening with a cotton-wool pattern.
Audiometry (same day, our audiology): right-sided conductive hearing loss.

Assessment: Paget disease of bone of the left tibia, with a raised alkaline phosphatase and normal calcium, PTH and vitamin D. Right conductive hearing loss.

Plan:
1. Needle biopsy of the left tibia to exclude any other process before treatment; scheduled 11/8.
2. If confirmed, a single zoledronic acid infusion. Please make sure he takes vitamin D and gets enough dietary calcium beforehand.
3. Alkaline phosphatase about 3 months after treatment.

Orthopedic surgery

reports.text:
Specimen: bone, left tibia, needle core biopsy.
Gross: two cores of tan-white bone, 1.4 and 1.1 cm, decalcified.
Microscopic: Thickened, irregular bony trabeculae with a mosaic pattern of cement lines. Increased numbers of osteoclasts, some large and multinucleated, with osteoblastic rimming. Intertrabecular fibrovascular marrow. No atypical cells. No malignancy.
reports.conclusion: Left tibia, needle biopsy: findings consistent with Paget disease of bone. Negative for malignancy.

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Came for BP but the real story: since around January more tired than he's ever been, naps afternoons. Fills up after half a plate, belt is looser. Wife thinks he's lost weight; scale here confirms, 92-93 all of last year, 88.5 today. No fevers or sweats he's noticed. No bleeding, no black stools. Cough at baseline. Leg better since the infusion.

Exam: tired-appearing but comfortable. Conjunctivae a little pale. No lymphadenopathy neck, axillae, groin. Abdomen: spleen edge firm and palpable well below the left costal margin, nontender. Liver not enlarged. Lungs with a few wheezes, his usual. No edema, no petechiae.

CBC this afternoon: Hgb 9.2, WBC 2.6, plt 84. All three lines low, which is new (CBC normal in 9/2021).

A/P
1. Fatigue, early satiety, weight loss with an enlarged spleen and low counts in all three lines. Needs hematology quickly. Urgent referral placed, called their office myself, they will see him 4/24. Reviewed with pt and wife by phone this afternoon; bleeding and fever precautions.
2. HTN, CKD 2: BP as charted. BMP today. No changes.
RTC after heme.

events.reason: Pancytopenia, splenomegaly, fatigue and weight loss

reports.text:
Specimen: bone marrow, right posterior iliac crest, aspirate attempt and trephine core.
Aspirate: no particles obtained (dry tap); touch preparations of the core made instead.
Core: 1.6 cm adequate core. Marrow largely replaced by fibrosis, with clusters of atypical megakaryocytes showing hyperchromatic, cloud-like nuclei. Reduced erythroid and granulocytic elements. Reticulin and trichrome stains confirm increased fibrosis. Dilated sinusoids with intrasinusoidal hematopoiesis. No increase in blasts by CD34. No metastatic carcinoma.
Molecular studies sent separately.
reports.conclusion: Bone marrow: fibrotic myeloproliferative neoplasm, consistent with primary myelofibrosis in the appropriate clinical setting.

documents.title: Hematology-Oncology Consultation
documents.author: hematology-oncology
documents.body:
Outside hematology-oncology clinic
Date of consultation: 04/24/2023 (letter includes results through 05/01)
Patient: Bernard Bennett, DOB 07/03/1955

Dear colleague,
Thank you for the urgent referral. Mr. Bennett is 67 and comes with his wife. Over three months he has grown steadily more tired, feels full after small meals, and has lost weight without trying. You found low counts and a large spleen on 4/11.

Background: hypertension, no prior cancer. Chronic bronchitis and Paget disease of the left tibia (zoledronic acid 12/2022). CKD, BPH, urethral stricture, lumbar spondylosis. Former smoker, 40 pack-years. Meds: hydrochlorothiazide, lisinopril, tamsulosin, vitamin D, acetaminophen PRN. NKDA.

Exam: pale, no jaundice. Marked splenomegaly reaching well below the left costal margin. No lymphadenopathy. No hepatomegaly.

Labs today: hemoglobin 9.0 g/dL, WBC 2,500/uL, platelets 80,000/uL. Smear reviewed personally: many teardrop red cells, occasional nucleated red cells and immature granulocytes (leukoerythroblastic picture). No circulating blasts of note.

Bone marrow 4/24: the aspirate was a dry tap, so a trephine core was taken in the same sitting. Pathology (5/1): marrow fibrosis with clustered atypical megakaryocytes, consistent with primary myelofibrosis. JAK2 V617F detected. Abdominal ultrasound 4/27: spleen 19 cm, liver normal in size.

Impression: JAK2-positive primary myelofibrosis with symptomatic splenomegaly, constitutional symptoms and cytopenias.

Plan: We discussed the nature of this disease with him and his wife. Given his age and other conditions he is not a candidate for stem cell transplant and we will focus on symptom control. I will see him on 5/10 to start a JAK inhibitor and go over its monitoring. We will do his blood counts here every few weeks at first, then about every three months.

With thanks,
Hematology-oncology

reports.text:
Indication: splenomegaly.
The spleen is enlarged, measuring 19 cm in craniocaudal length, with homogeneous echotexture and no focal lesion. Liver normal in size and echotexture, no focal lesion. Gallbladder without stones. Common bile duct not dilated. Kidneys normal in size without hydronephrosis. Pancreas partially obscured by bowel gas. No ascites.
reports.conclusion: Splenomegaly, 19 cm. Liver normal in size.

documents.title: Abdominal ultrasound (ordered by hematology)
documents.author: radiology
documents.body: Copy to primary care. Spleen 19 cm, homogeneous. Liver normal in size. No ascites.

events.reason: Start JAK inhibitor for primary myelofibrosis

medications.sig: Take 1 tablet by mouth twice daily

documents.title: Hematology Follow-up
documents.author: hematology-oncology
documents.body:
Hematology follow-up 05/10/2023, Mr. Bennett, primary myelofibrosis.
Symptoms unchanged: tired, early fullness. Counts similar to 4/24.
With platelets in the 80s, starting ruxolitinib at 5 mg twice daily. Reviewed common effects: lower blood counts, especially anemia early on, dizziness, bruising, infections including shingles (he has had both Shingrix doses), weight gain, raised cholesterol. Avoid starting strong CYP3A4 inhibitors without checking with us.
Through the specialty pharmacy. CBC in 4 weeks, visit in 3 months.
Current medications per patient: HCTZ 25, lisinopril 10, tamsulosin 0.4, vitamin D 1,000 units, acetaminophen as needed, now ruxolitinib 5 mg BID. NKDA.
Hematology-oncology

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Wife came in with him today, and asked to talk about memory.

Her account: over roughly the past year he misplaces his keys and glasses, blanks on the names of people they've met recently at church, and sometimes hunts for a word mid-sentence. He agrees, a bit embarrassed, says the old names are all there. He still does the bills, nothing late; fills his own pill box and hasn't missed doses by her count. Drives locally without getting lost. Sleep: up earlier than he used to, not tired in the day. Mood ok. Mother had dementia, which is why she's worried.

BP: 146/90 here. Home cuff he says mostly 130s/80s, no log with him.

Exam: alert, pleasant, gives a coherent history. Oriented. Recalls 2 of 3 words at 5 minutes, third with a cue. Clock drawing normal. Neuro nonfocal. Heart/lungs at baseline.

A/P
1. Memory complaints over a year, mostly recall and names, function intact. Refer neurology for a fuller evaluation; they'll decide on labs and testing.
2. HTN: above goal today. Hasn't been this high here before. Wants to try cutting salt and bring home readings before adding anything. Recheck at the fall visit.
3. CKD 2: BMP today.
4. Colon screening: due by date (last 2014). Talked through colonoscopy vs FIT given his platelets; he prefers FIT. Kit given.
5. PMF per heme.
RTC Sept for AWV.

documents.title: Neurology Consultation
documents.author: neurology
documents.body:
Outside neurology practice
Seen 04/24/2024
Re: Bernard Bennett, 68-year-old man

Reason: memory.

Mr. Bennett comes with his wife, who first noticed the change. Over about a year he has lost track of where he puts his keys, struggles to come up with names of people he has just met, and now and then cannot find the word he wants. He keeps up with community activities, pays the household bills on time and manages his own medications. His sleep has shifted earlier; he does not feel tired during the day.

Context: primary myelofibrosis diagnosed a year ago (ruxolitinib), Paget disease of the left tibia treated in 2022, chronic bronchitis, hypertension, CKD stage 2, BPH, urethral stricture, lumbar spondylosis. Former smoker. Mother had dementia.
Meds: hydrochlorothiazide 25, lisinopril 10, tamsulosin 0.4, ruxolitinib 5 BID, vitamin D, acetaminophen PRN. NKDA.

Exam: Alert and oriented to person, place and time. MMSE 28/30, both points lost on delayed recall. Language fluent, naming intact on formal testing. Cranial nerves, motor, sensory, reflexes, coordination and gait normal.

Labs today: electrolytes, TSH and B12 normal. CBC unchanged from the counts his hematologist follows.

Impression: Age-related cognitive decline. The pattern (retrieval of names and recent placements, preserved function, near-normal screening score) fits normal aging rather than a neurodegenerative process at this time.

Plan: Reassurance. Regular exercise, social engagement, sleep regularity, good blood pressure control. Return in six months to reassess.

Neurology

documents.title: Neurologist

documents.title: RE: Neurologist
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Good news, and I read her letter the same way. A family history raises the question but doesn't decide it; that's why the recheck in October makes sense. The best things he can do are what she said: keep moving, keep busy with people, and get the blood pressure down. Thank you for coming with him.

documents.title: Neurology Follow-up
documents.author: neurology
documents.body:
Neurology follow-up 10/07/2024, Mr. Bennett, 69.
Booked as a six-month memory recheck; today's visit was taken up by a new leg problem.

For two weeks he has had a dull ache in the front of the right thigh that sometimes runs toward the inner knee. Walking uphill brings it on and rest relieves it. The right leg feels weaker getting up from a chair or stepping up onto a curb. No bowel or bladder incontinence, no saddle numbness, no back trauma. Long history of lumbar arthritis. Blood pressure has been running high at his primary care visits.

Meds: hydrochlorothiazide, lisinopril, tamsulosin, ruxolitinib, vitamin D, acetaminophen. NKDA.

Exam: Right knee extension 4/5; hip flexion and ankle dorsiflexion/plantarflexion full. Right patellar reflex reduced relative to the left; ankle jerks symmetric. Pinprick and light touch diminished over the right anterior thigh and medial shin. Straight leg raise negative bilaterally. Gait slightly guarded.

Impression: Right lumbar radiculopathy, L4 distribution, on a background of lumbar spondylosis. No red flags.

Plan: MRI lumbar spine without contrast. Acetaminophen as he is using. Will call with results and arrange therapy. Memory recheck deferred to next visit.

Neurology

reports.text:
Indication: right anterior thigh pain and knee extension weakness.
Technique: Multiplanar multisequence MRI of the lumbar spine without contrast.
Alignment: normal lordosis, no listhesis. Vertebral body heights preserved. No fracture. Conus terminates at L1, normal.
L1-L2, L2-L3: mild disc desiccation, no stenosis.
L3-L4: disc desiccation and height loss with a right subarticular disc bulge and facet hypertrophy narrowing the right lateral recess, contacting the traversing right L4 nerve root. No significant central canal stenosis. Foramina patent.
L4-L5: disc degeneration and facet arthropathy, mild bilateral foraminal narrowing without root contact.
L5-S1: disc degeneration and facet arthropathy, no stenosis.
Paraspinal soft tissues unremarkable.
reports.conclusion: Multilevel lumbar degenerative disease L3-S1. Right L3-L4 lateral recess narrowing contacting the traversing right L4 root.

Regional emergency department, visit 04/17/2025
Patient: Bernard Bennett, 69 M

Chief complaint: blood in urine.

HPI: This morning he saw red urine at the start of urinating that cleared by the end of the stream. One episode so far. History of urethral stricture dilated in 2019. No injury, no heavy exercise. No flank pain, fever or dysuria.
PMH: urethral stricture, BPH, hypertension, CKD, primary myelofibrosis on ruxolitinib, chronic bronchitis, Paget disease of left tibia, lumbar spondylosis.
Meds: hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg daily, acetaminophen 500 mg PRN; reports tamsulosin and lisinopril as well; ruxolitinib 5 mg BID; vitamin D. NKDA.

Vitals: BP 145/90, HR 78, afebrile.
Exam: Abdomen soft, nontender, no flank tenderness. GU: prostate mildly enlarged, nontender on rectal exam. Meatus without discharge or lesions.

Results: UA with red cells present (blood moderate, 35 RBC/hpf), no casts, nitrite and leukocyte esterase negative. Creatinine 1.1 mg/dL. CBC at his known baseline per his hematology history, unchanged. PT/INR within normal range.

MDM: Initial hematuria, which points to a urethral source, in a man with a known stricture. Kidney function stable. No clot retention; voided comfortably here.
Disposition: home. Outpatient urology for cystoscopy and upper tract imaging. Return for clots, inability to void, fever.

Emergency medicine

Outside urology, 05/13/2025
Re: Bernard Bennett

Mr. Bennett returns to us, last seen for dilation of a bulbar urethral stricture in August 2019. He had one episode of initial hematuria on 4/17, seen in the ED, none since. Voiding adequately, no retention.
Meds: tamsulosin, lisinopril, hydrochlorothiazide, ruxolitinib, vitamin D. NKDA.

CT urogram 5/6: no upper tract or bladder lesion.

Flexible cystoscopy today under topical anesthesia: short bulbar urethral stricture, narrow but the scope passes; the mucosa at the stricture is friable and oozes slightly on contact. Prostatic lateral lobes enlarged. Bladder fully inspected: no tumor, no stones, no diverticula. Tolerated well.

Assessment: initial hematuria from a friable recurrent bulbar stricture. Upper tracts and bladder clear. BPH.
Plan: he voids adequately and prefers to avoid another procedure now; observation. Continue tamsulosin. Repeat urinalysis at his primary care office in a few weeks. Return if stream worsens, retention, or further bleeding.

documents.title: Emergency Department Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Regional emergency department, 10/10/2025
Patient: Bernard Bennett, 70 M

CC: passed out while shaving.

HPI: Over recent months he has had repeated short dizzy spells. This morning, razor at his neck, he felt light-headed, then everything went dark and he came to on the bathroom floor; his wife heard him fall. Out for seconds, no incontinence, no tongue biting, oriented right away. No chest pain or palpitations beforehand. No injury.
PMH: hypertension, CKD, BPH, urethral stricture, primary myelofibrosis (ruxolitinib), chronic bronchitis, Paget disease of left tibia, lumbar spondylosis, age-related cognitive decline.
Meds: hydrochlorothiazide 25, lisinopril 10, tamsulosin 0.4, acetaminophen PRN, ruxolitinib 5 BID, vitamin D. NKDA.

Vitals: BP 145/90, HR 78.
Exam: alert, oriented. Neurological exam normal. No carotid bruits. Heart regular, no murmur.
ECG: normal sinus rhythm, normal intervals. Troponin normal. BMP normal. CBC at his known baseline.

With continuous ECG and arterial pressure monitoring and atropine at the bedside, carotid sinus massage was performed (right side, 5 seconds; no bruits on auscultation beforehand). It produced a 4-second ventricular pause and a fall in systolic pressure to 85 mm Hg, reproducing his light-headedness. Recovered fully within seconds.

Impression: Syncope due to carotid sinus hypersensitivity, mixed cardioinhibitory and vasodepressor response.
Disposition: observed, ambulating without symptoms, discharged with his wife. Advised to avoid pressure on the neck and tight collars, use an electric razor, and turn his head slowly. Cardiology referral via his primary care. Return for recurrent syncope.

Emergency medicine

documents.title: Hospital Discharge Summary
documents.author: critical care medicine
documents.body:
Regional medical center
Admitted 04/12/2026, discharged 04/18/2026
Patient: Bernard Bennett, 70 M
Service: medical ICU, then medicine floor

Principal diagnosis: Hypertensive emergency.
Secondary: Cyanide toxicity from sodium nitroprusside. Acute rise in creatinine on chronic kidney disease with the hypertensive emergency.
Chronic: hypertension, chronic kidney disease, mild neurocognitive disorder, primary myelofibrosis on ruxolitinib, carotid sinus hypersensitivity, chronic bronchitis, BPH, urethral stricture, Paget disease of left tibia, lumbar spondylosis.
Allergies: NKDA.

Course:
He came to the ED on the evening of 4/12 with a severe headache and a blood pressure of 226/128. Creatinine 2.5, BUN 40. With renal involvement this was treated as a hypertensive emergency and he went to the ICU on a sodium nitroprusside infusion.

After about 48 hours on nitroprusside (4/14), nursing reported that he had become steadily more agitated and confused. He described a severe headache and looked flushed, and his wife thought he was breathing harder than normal. BP 145/90, HR 102, RR 22, SpO2 94% on room air. Arterial gas pH 7.35, PaCO2 45, PaO2 85. Na 140, K 4.2, creatinine 2.8 (2.5 on admission), BUN 55, lactate 5 mmol/L. ECG: sinus tachycardia without other abnormality. Venous cyanide sent.

Cyanide toxicity was diagnosed clinically. Nitroprusside was stopped, hydroxocobalamin 5 g IV was given, and blood pressure control was switched to a nicardipine infusion. Lactate 1.6 the next morning. Confusion and headache cleared within a day and his wife felt he was back to himself. The cyanide level returned 4/16 at 1.1 mg/L, confirming the diagnosis.

He transitioned to oral therapy; amlodipine 5 mg daily added to his home regimen. Creatinine improved to 1.6 by discharge. BP at discharge 142/86.

Discharge medications:
- amlodipine 5 mg daily (NEW)
- lisinopril 10 mg daily
- hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg daily
- tamsulosin 0.4 mg daily
- ruxolitinib 5 mg twice daily
- vitamin D3 1,000 units daily
- acetaminophen 500 mg as needed

Follow-up: primary care within one week with a BMP. Hematology as scheduled.

Critical care / hospital medicine

documents.title: Post-discharge call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Transitional care call, 2 business days after discharge. Spoke with pt and wife. Home since Saturday. Headache gone, thinking clear, wife agrees. Picked up amlodipine; reviewed full med list against the discharge summary, matches. Home BP this morning 136/82. Visit booked Friday 4/24 with BMP. ED for severe headache, confusion, chest pain or BP over 180.

documents.title: Hospital Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
TCM visit. Discharge summary reviewed in full.
Admitted 4/12-4/18: hypertensive emergency (226/128, creatinine 2.5), treated with nitroprusside in the ICU; at 48 h developed agitation, confusion, headache, flushing and a lactate of 5; cyanide toxicity, confirmed by a level of 1.1. Nitroprusside stopped, hydroxocobalamin, nicardipine, then orals with amlodipine 5 added. Creatinine 2.8 at worst, 1.6 at discharge.

Today: feels himself again, wife agrees he's back to his usual. No headache. Taking all meds including the amlodipine. No dizziness or fainting.
Home BP 130s/80s.

Exam: BP 138/84. Alert, conversational, oriented, at his baseline. Heart regular. Lungs baseline. No edema.
Lab today: creatinine 1.4, potassium normal.

A/P
1. Hypertensive emergency, resolved. Now on amlodipine 5 + lisinopril 10 + HCTZ 25. Watch for light-headedness given carotid sinus hypersensitivity; so far fine.
2. Cyanide toxicity from nitroprusside, resolved without lasting deficit. Documented in the problem list so any future admission sees it.
3. CKD 2 with the creatinine still coming down from the admission. Repeat at June visit.
4. PMF, heme in May.
Med reconciliation done. RTC 6-7 weeks.

Now well. Spleen unchanged. CBC at his baseline; creatinine improving.
Continue ruxolitinib 5 mg twice daily. Return August.

documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Follow-up after April admission.
Doing well. No headaches, no dizziness, no fainting. No blood in urine. Walking daily. Memory unchanged per wife. Taking amlodipine, lisinopril, HCTZ, tamsulosin, ruxolitinib, vitamin D.
Home BP log (finally written down): 124-136 / 74-84.

Exam: BP 132/80, at goal for the first time in two years. Heart regular. Lungs scattered wheezes, baseline. Spleen tip palpable, unchanged. No edema. Neuro nonfocal.

A/P
1. HTN at goal on three agents. Continue amlodipine 5.
2. CKD 2: creatinine back to 1.2 today. UACR sent.
3. Carotid sinus hypersensitivity: no recurrence, precautions continue.
4. PMF: heme following, August visit.
5. HM: AWV in September, flu and COVID then, FIT due, CT in November.
RTC September.
